_comment: The tower: Ryan's hand-modelled TowerRock, with the watch chamber's wall SCULPTED OUT OF IT by tower_build.py -- his rim loop and his cap loop are resampled onto one bearing set and bridged, so the room wall is his own silhouette continued rather than a ring stuck on. ORIGIN IS THE ROOM'S FLOOR -- the guard stands at local y=0; the rock hangs to y=-37.3 and the cap top is at +9.6. One textured material (packed 128x128 atlas + emissive), one UV set, no skin, no animation. TowerCollision is the purpose-built collider that rides in the .glb as a `-colonly` node: Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and discards its mesh, which is why `surfaces` is still 1 and `max_tris` counts only what is drawn. If TowerCollision ever stops appearing, the model has silently gone back to having no collision and the guard will fall through the floor.
